regimes.name: International Traffic in Arms Regulations and U.S. Munitions List
regimes.administrator: Department of State, Directorate of Defense Trade Controls
regimes.summary: Controls the export and temporary import of defense articles, technical data and defense services listed on the USML (Categories I-XXI).

key_provisions.text: USML Categories I (firearms), II (guns and armament), III (ammunition and ordnance), IV (missiles, rockets, bombs, mines), VII (ground vehicles), VIII (aircraft, incl. unmanned), XI (military electronics), XII (fire control, laser, imaging, guidance), XIX (gas turbine engines), among others.
Defense service: furnishing assistance, including training, to foreign persons in the design, production, operation, repair or use of defense articles.

Technical data: information (other than software as defined) required for the design, development, production, operation, repair, testing, maintenance or modification of defense articles; excludes general scientific principles taught in schools and public-domain information.

Public domain: information that is published and generally accessible through listed channels (bookstores, libraries, open conferences, patents, government-approved public release, fundamental research).

changes.text: Rule effective that moved most non-automatic and semi-automatic firearms and related items from USML Categories I-III to the EAR (State rule 85 FR 3819; Commerce rule 85 FR 4136, both published 23 Jan 2020).
Part 120 reorganization effective (87 FR 16396). Definitions renumbered: defense service now 120.32 (was 120.9), technical data now 120.33 (was 120.10), public domain now 120.34.
USML targeted revisions effective (published 17 Jan 2025 as 90 FR 5594; effective date set by 90 FR 41778).

regimes.notes: Silencers and suppressors (Cat. I(e)) and fully automatic firearms (Cat. I(b)) remained on the USML after the 2020 transfer. Neither the USML nor the Wassenaar Munitions List uses the term 'loitering munition' (text search, 6 Oct 2026).

regimes.name: Arms Export Control Act, section 38
regimes.administrator: President, delegated to the Department of State
regimes.summary: Authorizes the President to control the export and import of defense articles and defense services and to designate the items that make up the USML. It is the statutory basis for the ITAR.

key_provisions.text: President authorized to control import and export of defense articles and services and to designate them.
Designation of items as defense articles is not subject to judicial review. The Ninth Circuit read this to bar review of both designation and removal (Washington v. Dep't of State, 2021).

regimes.name: Export Administration Regulations and Commerce Control List (600-series and 0x5zz firearms entries)
regimes.cite: 15 CFR parts 730-774; CCL at Supp. No. 1 to part 774
regimes.administrator: Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security
regimes.summary: Controls dual-use items and less sensitive military items. Since March 2020 it covers most non-automatic and semi-automatic firearms, their ammunition, and related software and technology.

key_provisions.text: 0A501: non-automatic firearms and related items. 0A506-0A508: semi-automatic rifles, pistols and shotguns. 0A509: certain parts and accessories for them.
Ammunition for firearms controlled on the CCL.
Software and technology for development, production, operation or maintenance of 0A501, 0A506, 0A507, 0A509 and 0B501 items.
Unclassified technology or software is 'published', and so not subject to the EAR, when made available to the public without restriction, including posting on public internet sites.

Exception: software or technology for producing a firearm, frame or receiver (ECCNs 0A501, 0A506, 0A507, 0A509) posted online in a format ready for insertion into a CNC machine tool or additive manufacturing equipment remains subject to the EAR.
Unmanned aerial vehicles designed for controlled flight beyond the operator's natural vision. Missile technology (MT) controls apply to UAVs capable of at least 300 km range regardless of payload.
Military ground vehicles and related items not enumerated on the USML.

changes.text: Firearms transfer from USML Categories I-III takes effect; 734.7(c) added (85 FR 4136).
BIS interim final rule 'Revision of Firearms License Requirements' (89 FR 34680) tightened firearm export licensing and created ECCNs 0A506-0A509.
BIS final rule (90 FR 47170) rescinded the 2024 interim rule except for the new ECCNs, and removed the congressional notification requirement for certain semi-automatic firearm licence applications.

regimes.notes: Classification of a specific item depends on its technical parameters. This page does not classify any real product.

regimes.name: National Firearms Act
regimes.summary: Requires registration and taxes the making and transfer of listed 'firearms': short-barreled rifles and shotguns, machineguns, silencers, destructive devices and 'any other weapons'.

key_provisions.text: Defines NFA 'firearm' (incl. machinegun and silencer) and 'machinegun' (fires automatically more than one shot by a single function of the trigger, incl. conversion parts).
Makes it unlawful to possess or receive an NFA firearm that is unregistered or transferred or made in violation of the chapter.
Transfer tax: $200 for machineguns and destructive devices; $0 for other NFA firearms (as amended in 2025).

changes.text: Pub. L. 119-21, sec. 70436 cut the transfer tax to $0 for NFA firearms other than machineguns and destructive devices (e.g. suppressors, short-barreled rifles), for calendar quarters beginning more than 90 days after enactment. Registration requirements were not removed.

regimes.name: Gun Control Act of 1968, incl. 18 U.S.C. 922(o)
regimes.summary: Licensing of manufacturers, importers and dealers, background checks, serial marking and transfer rules. Section 922(o) bars private transfer or possession of machineguns not lawfully possessed before the provision took effect.

key_provisions.text: Defines 'firearm' to include a weapon designed to or readily convertible to expel a projectile by explosive action, and the frame or receiver of such a weapon.
Unlawful to transfer or possess a machinegun, except for government use or machineguns lawfully possessed before the subsection took effect.

regimes.name: ATF rule: Definition of 'Frame or Receiver' and Identification of Firearms (2022)
regimes.summary: Interprets the GCA to cover weapon parts kits that can readily be converted to a working firearm and partially complete frames or receivers, bringing them under licensing, background-check, record and serial-number rules.

key_provisions.text: Definition of frame or receiver, incl. partially complete, disassembled or nonfunctional frames or receivers.

changes.text: Rule effective (published 26 Apr 2022).
Bondi v. VanDerStok, No. 23-852: Supreme Court (7-2, Gorsuch, J.) held the rule is not facially inconsistent with the GCA. The Court noted some kits may be too incomplete to qualify.

Defense Distributed v. Blanche (N.D. Tex.): district court reportedly held the challenged provisions unconstitutionally vague and contrary to the Second Amendment. Remedy scope and appeal status not verified here.

regimes.notes: The 2026 district court ruling is reported by a secondary source; read the opinion before relying on it.

regimes.name: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems
regimes.summary: Requires autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems to be designed so commanders and operators can exercise appropriate levels of human judgment over the use of force, and sets a senior review process for autonomous systems outside its exemptions.

key_provisions.text: Defines an autonomous weapon system as one that, once activated, can select and engage targets without further intervention by an operator. The directive does not apply to unarmed platforms, unguided munitions, operator-guided munitions or mines.

changes.text: Updated directive issued, replacing the 2012 version.
NSPM-11, 'Artificial Intelligence in the National Security Enterprise', directs DoD to update 3000.09 within 90 days and review it annually. No revised directive verified as of 6 Oct 2026.

regimes.notes: The official PDF (esd.whs.mil) blocks automated retrieval; content verified through the Congressional Research Service primer IF11150 (updated 26 Mar 2026).

sources.label: CRS IF11150, Defense Primer: U.S. Policy on Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems

regimes.name: FAA small UAS rule and statutory ban on weaponized drones
regimes.summary: Part 107 governs civil operation of small unmanned aircraft (under 55 lb). Section 363 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 bars operating any unmanned aircraft equipped or armed with a dangerous weapon unless the FAA authorizes it.

key_provisions.text: Small unmanned aircraft: under 55 pounds on takeoff, including everything on board.
No operating a UAS equipped or armed with a dangerous weapon (18 U.S.C. 930(g)(2)) unless authorized by the FAA Administrator; civil penalty up to $25,000 per violation.

changes.text: FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 enacted, incl. § 363.

regimes.notes: Section 363 is an uncodified note to 49 U.S.C. 44802, not a numbered section of title 49.

sources.label: FAA, 'Drones and Weapons, A Dangerous Mix' (22 Aug 2019)

regimes.name: Wassenaar Arrangement (Munitions List and Dual-Use List)
regimes.force: Politically binding; implemented through national law
regimes.summary: Participating States apply export controls to items on the Munitions List (ML1-ML22) and the List of Dual-Use Goods and Technologies. National implementation dates vary.

key_provisions.text: ML1 smooth-bore weapons under 20 mm, other arms and automatic weapons; ML2 larger-calibre weapons; ML3 ammunition; ML4 bombs, rockets, missiles and other explosive devices.
ML5 fire control and warning equipment; ML6 ground vehicles; ML10 aircraft and UAVs; ML15 imaging or countermeasure equipment.
Software and technology. Technology 'in the public domain' (made available without restrictions on further dissemination) is excluded from ML22.

changes.text: 2025 Plenary amendments incorporated into the current lists (published Jan 2026).

regimes.name: Missile Technology Control Regime
regimes.force: Politically binding; implemented through national law
regimes.cite: MTCR Guidelines and Equipment, Software and Technology Annex
regimes.summary: Category I covers complete rocket and unmanned air vehicle systems (incl. cruise missiles and target or reconnaissance drones) able to carry at least 500 kg to at least 300 km, plus major subsystems and production facilities. Category II covers other systems with 300 km range and a wide set of components.

key_provisions.text: Particular restraint for Category I transfers 'and there will be a strong presumption to deny such transfers'. Category I production facilities will not be authorized until further notice.
Category I: 300 km / 500 kg range-payload threshold. Category II: complete systems with 300 km range not in Category I, and many dual-use items.

changes.text: US State Department announced it will review exports of advanced UAS similar to manned fighter aircraft rather than under the stricter missile approach, as a US reinterpretation of MTCR commitments.

regimes.notes: The 2025 change is a US national policy; the MTCR Annex text itself was not reported as amended.

regimes.name: Arms Trade Treaty
regimes.cite: New York, 2 April 2013; in force 24 Dec 2014
regimes.summary: Requires States Parties to regulate transfers of eight categories of conventional arms, plus their ammunition and parts, and to deny transfers that would breach embargoes or risk serious violations.

key_provisions.text: Scope: battle tanks; armoured combat vehicles; large-calibre artillery; combat aircraft; attack helicopters; warships; missiles and launchers; small arms and light weapons.
National control systems for exports of ammunition/munitions and of parts and components for covered arms.
Prohibits authorizing transfers that would violate UN Security Council Chapter VII measures, such as arms embargoes, or other international obligations.

regimes.notes: UN Treaty Collection status (6 Oct 2026): 130 signatories, 118 parties. The United States signed in 2013 and later notified the depositary that it does not intend to become a party.

regimes.name: UN Programme of Action on Small Arms and Light Weapons and International Tracing Instrument
regimes.summary: Sets out national, regional and global steps against illicit trade in small arms and light weapons; the ITI covers marking and record-keeping so weapons can be traced.

key_provisions.text: Adopted 2001. Steps include laws and administrative procedures to control SALW production and transfer, record-keeping, criminalizing illegal manufacture and trade, marking, and destroying surplus.
Steps for marking and record-keeping so illicit SALW can be traced.

regimes.notes: Both instruments are politically, not legally, binding.

regimes.name: Protocol against the Illicit Manufacturing of and Trafficking in Firearms (supplementing UNTOC)
regimes.cite: New York, 31 May 2001; in force 3 July 2005
regimes.summary: Criminal-justice treaty on illicit manufacturing and trafficking of firearms, their parts and ammunition, incl. marking, record-keeping and import/export authorization.

key_provisions.text: Import, export and transit licensing. The EU implements Art. 10 through Regulation (EU) No 258/2012.

sources.label: UN Treaty Collection, Firearms Protocol status

regimes.name: Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons and Protocols; GGE on lethal autonomous weapon systems
regimes.force: Legally binding on High Contracting Parties; GGE outputs are not binding
regimes.summary: Framework treaty with protocols restricting specific weapons: Protocols I-III (1980), IV on blinding laser weapons (1995), II as amended on mines, booby-traps and other devices (1996), V on explosive remnants of war (2003). Hosts the Group of Governmental Experts on lethal autonomous weapon systems.

key_provisions.text: Restrictions on mines, booby-traps and other devices.
GGE mandate: further consider and formulate, by consensus, a set of elements of an instrument, without prejudging its nature, and report to the Seventh Review Conference.

changes.text: GGE on LAWS adopted by consensus a report completing its 2024-2026 mandate, containing a set of elements of an instrument (paras. 25-44). It goes to the Seventh Review Conference in November 2026; no negotiating mandate exists yet.

regimes.notes: UN Treaty Collection status (6 Oct 2026): 128 parties to the Convention.

regimes.name: UN General Assembly resolutions on lethal autonomous weapons systems
regimes.summary: Three annual resolutions on autonomous weapons. The 2025 text calls on CCW parties to complete the elements of an instrument with a view to future negotiation.

key_provisions.text: Adopted 22 Dec 2023: 152 in favour, 4 against, 11 abstentions.
Adopted 2 Dec 2024: 166 in favour, 3 against, 15 abstentions.
Adopted 1 Dec 2025: 164 in favour, 6 against (incl. the United States and Russia), 7 abstentions.

regimes.notes: Vote counts from un-project.org, which mirrors UN Digital Library voting records; UN record for A/RES/80/57: digitallibrary.un.org/record/4095989.

sources.label: Stop Killer Robots on First Committee vote (6 Nov 2025)

regimes.name: Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention
regimes.summary: As its full title states, prohibits the use, stockpiling, production and transfer of anti-personnel mines and provides for their destruction.

key_provisions.text: Withdrawal takes effect six months after notification.

changes.text: Withdrawals of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania took effect.
Withdrawal of Finland took effect.
Withdrawal of Poland took effect.

regimes.notes: UN Treaty Collection status (6 Oct 2026): 162 parties. The status page does not record a withdrawal by Ukraine.

sources.label: UN Treaty Collection, Ottawa Convention status and notes

regimes.name: Convention on Cluster Munitions
regimes.summary: Prohibits use, development, production, acquisition, stockpiling, retention and transfer of cluster munitions as defined in the Convention.

key_provisions.text: Each State Party undertakes never to use cluster munitions; develop, produce, otherwise acquire, stockpile, retain or transfer them; or assist anyone in prohibited activity.
Withdrawal takes effect six months after notification.

changes.text: Withdrawal of Lithuania took effect.

regimes.notes: UN Treaty Collection status (6 Oct 2026): 112 parties.

regimes.name: Council Common Position 2008/944/CFSP on exports of military technology and equipment
regimes.cite: Common Position 2008/944/CFSP (8 Dec 2008), amended by Decision (CFSP) 2019/1560
regimes.administrator: EU Member States (Council Working Party COARM)
regimes.summary: Member States assess licence applications for items on the EU Common Military List case by case against the criteria in Article 2, starting with international obligations such as sanctions and embargoes.

key_provisions.text: Case-by-case assessment against Article 2 criteria; Member States encouraged to reassess licences when new information arises.

changes.text: Decision (CFSP) 2019/1560 amended the Common Position after a Council review.

regimes.notes: EUR-Lex was not fully available on 6 Oct 2026; text checked through legislation.gov.uk (EU-origin archive) and a Council document.

regimes.name: Regulation (EU) 2021/821 on dual-use items
regimes.summary: Common EU export control rules for dual-use items: shared assessment criteria, authorization types, a common EU dual-use list and end-use controls. Military-list items fall under national law and the Common Position instead.

key_provisions.text: EU dual-use control list, updated by delegated regulation to track regime changes.

changes.text: Commission adopted a Delegated Regulation updating the Annex I list.

regimes.name: Firearms Directive (EU) 2021/555 and Firearms Regulation (EU) No 258/2012
regimes.force: Binding (Directive via national law; Regulation directly applicable)
regimes.summary: The Directive sets minimum common rules on acquisition and possession of civilian firearms and intra-EU transfers. The Regulation governs export, import and transit of civilian firearms, parts and ammunition and does not apply to firearms for military or police use.

key_provisions.text: Minimum rules on acquisition, possession and intra-EU transfer of civilian firearms.
Export, import and transit of civilian firearms; implements Art. 10 of the UN Firearms Protocol.

changes.text: Commission proposed a recast of the Firearms Regulation (status not checked here).
